question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,v.$ Find $(u-3v+5w)\cdot u.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot v=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u-3v+5w)\cdot u & =u\cdot u-3(v\cdot u)+5(w\cdot u) \\  & =u\cdot u-0+5(w\cdot u) \\  & =u\cdot u+5(w\cdot u) \\  & =((-2)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 1+0\cdot 0+1\cdot 1) \\  & +5(2\cdot (-2)+0\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 1) \\  & =(4+1+0+1)+5(-4+0+0-1) \\  & =6-25 \\  & =-19.\end{aligned}
$$
